Equal housing opportunity

Fair housing

Every home I manage is offered to everyone on the same terms.

I follow federal, Washington and King County fair housing law when I advertise a place, when I screen the people who ask about it, and when I rent it. Here's who those laws protect, and what to do if something doesn't feel right.

Who the law protects If something doesn't feel right

Who the law protects

Three sets of rules cover a home on Vashon: federal law, Washington law, and King County's code, which applies in unincorporated King County. That includes Vashon-Maury Island. I follow all three. Each list is as that law words it.

    $class_cards

Source of income

I welcome housing choice vouchers and every other lawful source of income.

Washington counts housing assistance, public assistance, emergency rental assistance, veterans benefits, Social Security, Supplemental Security Income and other retirement programs, and other programs run by federal, state, local or nonprofit organizations. Income from illegal activity isn't included.

If I ask for a minimum income, I take any rent voucher or subsidy off the monthly rent first, and then check your income against what's left (RCW 59.18.255(3)). And I never advertise a preference for or against any source of income (RCW 59.18.255(2)).

Accommodations

If a disability means a rule, a policy or the home itself has to work differently for you, tell me. Washington law (RCW 49.60.222(2)) and King County's code (K.C.C. 12.20.040.E) both treat refusing a reasonable accommodation to a rule or policy, or a reasonable modification to the home, as discrimination. Service animals are welcome. Ask me and we'll work it out.

Screening

I use the same written criteria for every applicant, and I share them in writing before I pull any screening report, as Washington requires (RCW 59.18.257).

If something doesn't feel right

Please tell me first. Write to me@ebberry.com and say what happened. I read every note myself, and I'd rather make it right.

You can also go straight to an agency, without talking to me first. Each has a time limit for filing, so please don't wait. And nobody should be treated differently for raising a concern: retaliation is against the law.
